about: INDIRECT (docs/specs/exsheet-functions ticket 18; ADR-0124's notes of 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-12): A1-style text naming a cell or a range of the same Sheet, with or without its own qualifier, read as it stands after the recalculation (volatile). Its text is not rewritten by an insertion or a deletion. The forms the seventeenth Windows run and the area pass of 2026-10-12 observed are read as Excel reads them: R1C1 text (a1 FALSE, 0, a blank or left empty) naming an absolute cell or a range of two (R3C2, R2C2:R5C2), an offset in brackets from the Formula's own cell (R[1]C[-1]), a row part alone (R3) and a column part alone (C2); a structured reference's text as the typed Table[Column] is read; and A1# as the typed A1# is. The R1C1 forms that follow from those by the rule they settle are the engine's answers, which INDIRECT-045 to INDIRECT-050 ask: R and C each with a number or an offset in brackets, a row part alone a whole row, a column part alone a whole column, and two parts of the same kind joined by ':' the rectangle they span. #VALUE! until a run observes them, since the observed forms leave Excel's answer open: in R1C1 style, an R or a C with no number (RC[-1], R[2]C; INDIRECT-044, INDIRECT-051, INDIRECT-066), a zero offset in brackets (R[0], R[-0]; INDIRECT-064, INDIRECT-065), a number written with a leading 0 (INDIRECT-059), an offset written with a + (INDIRECT-063), an offset past the Sheet's edge, which Excel might call no place or wrap round to the far side (INDIRECT-052), a cell joined to a whole row or column (INDIRECT-058), a row joined to a column (INDIRECT-062), and structured or # text in R1C1 style (INDIRECT-060, INDIRECT-061); and a declared Linked Table's bare name (INDIRECT-053 to INDIRECT-057 ask what it reads). Text that names no place is #REF!: a number past the Sheet's edge, as XFE1 is (INDIRECT-017), another Sheet's name, and a table or column that does not exist.
